conviction_note: Nothing I found is an unpriced company-level number that decides this print. The company has beaten its own margin and EBITDA guides by wide margins two quarters running, which leans up. Against that, the bad news (Neutron slipping to 2027) was pre-released on 2026-10-14, the stock is up about 27% in three sessions from the 2026-11-04 close of $45.99 to spot $58.41, skew is +9.4 (downside paid), and the last record-backlog EBITDA beat traded flat (-0.04%). So p_up is 49 and abs_move is 9.5, above the 8.27% event-implied move because a Q4 guide and Neutron 2027 timing are both new and realised vol is 107%. The findings net to about zero and the scaled number is about zero; they agree.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue: company guide $250-265M (midpoint $257.5M; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000061/rklb-08102026ex991.htm). Consensus is $257.2M per MarketBeat (via https://www.tradingkey.com/analysis/stocks/us-stocks/262294990-rocketlab-neutron-rklb-spacex-tradingkey) and about $256.5M per Earnings Whispers (https://finviz.com/news/413866/rocket-labs-q3-report-puts-neutrons-narrowing-launch-window-ahead-of-record-revenue). The two sources agree and sit on the guide midpoint. Adj. EBITDA guide is a loss of $17-23M; GAAP gross margin guide 29-31% (non-GAAP 35-37%). The EPS bar is disputed: -$0.07 (MarketBeat) against -$0.02 non-GAAP with a -$0.01 whisper (Earnings Whispers), so nothing is sized on EPS. No sourced Q4 revenue consensus was found. The only full-year figure seen, Webull's $892M, is undated and implies a Q4 below Q3, so it is treated as stale.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 44-45M shares, about 7.3% of float, about 2.0-2.1 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement (equibles / marketbeat via search: https://equibles.com/stocks/rklb/shortinterest, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/RKLB/short-interest). No October settlement was found. This is not a crowded short. Skew is +9.44 vol points (25d put IV over 25d call IV), so downside is paid. Put/call OI is 0.79. ATM IV is 132% and the straddle implies 12.28% to the 11-13 expiry; the event-implied move is 8.27% (Money Morning quotes about 15%). Into the print the stock fell 12.2% on 11-05 in the post-election sell-off of high-beta growth, rose 15.4% on 11-06 to $53.07 and was up about 9% intraday on 11-09 to $58.41: a 27% bounce off the 11-04 close of $45.99 in three sessions, still 61% below the 52-week high of about $150 set on 2026-05-27.

findings.finding: Rocket Lab has beaten its own profitability guide by wide margins two quarters running, which points to a Q3 beat on the EBITDA loss (guided $17-23M) and on gross margin (guided 29-31%), though the market expects it. Q1 2026: adj. EBITDA loss $11.8M against a guided $21-27M, GAAP GM 38.2% against 34-36%. Q2 2026: EBITDA loss $8.8M against a guided $20-26M, GAAP GM about 36% against 33-35%. Revenue has landed at or above the guide midpoint: Q2 $234.1M against $225-240M, Q1 $200.3M against a $189.6M consensus. The Street EPS bar is split between -$0.07 and -$0.02, with a -$0.01 whisper, so part of the beat is expected.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-10): EBITDA beat the guide by about $14M at the midpoint, with record revenue and record backlog; the stock moved -0.04%. Q1 2026 (2026-05-07): revenue beat consensus by 5.6% plus a margin beat; +34.22%, the only big reaction in the five-print history. The other three prints: -4.89%, -1.27%, +1.09%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. If it were fully priced, consensus EPS would sit at the guide-implied number plus the usual beat, and Earnings Whispers' -$0.02 / -$0.01 whisper suggests it largely does. MarketBeat's -$0.07 has not moved. A beat on the EBITDA guide is the expected outcome, not a surprise.
findings.independence: Q1 guide and actuals come from the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000027/rklb-05072026ex991.htm); the Q2 guide-versus-actual comparison is restated by Earnings Whispers (https://finviz.com/news/413866/). Both rest on company documents.

findings.finding: Backlog at Q3-end should be a record, and the company has effectively pre-disclosed it. Backlog was $2.36B at 2026-06-30 (Space Systems $1.42B, Launch $940M), and the Q2 release says more than $1B of new Q3 contracts were signed, including deals after quarter-end: $266M for HASTE suborbital launches for the Space Force (2026-07-27), $397M for SB-AMTI Flatellite (2026-08-04) and more than $160M for three GEO satellites. Net of about $257M of Q3 revenue, that implies roughly $3.0-3.2B, against $2.36B.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed record backlog of $2.36B, up 137% y/y, and the stock moved -0.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced, because the contracts were announced individually and the release flagged the more than $1B of Q3 bookings. What is not public is the exact backlog figure and how much of it converts in the next 12 months (about 45% at Q2). A backlog well above about $3.1B would mean bookings beyond what was announced.
findings.independence: The individual awards were reported separately: https://thedefensepost.com/2026/07/29/rocket-lab-us-launch-contract/ for the $266M award. The same company release underlies the backlog figure.

findings.finding: Electron cadence in Q3 was flat and Q4 so far is slow. Company and press counts give 12 launches by 2026-06-27 (mission 91), 16 by 09-11 (mission 95), 17 by 09-19 (mission 96) and mission 97 on 09-26 (Synspective), so Q3 had 6 missions, the same as Q1 (6 by 03-28) and Q2 (6). Q2 launch revenue was $44.6M on 6 missions. In Q4 to date: mission 98 on about 10-21/23, mission 99 (WADATSUMI-II) about 11-03, and the 100th not before 11-14. So Q3 revenue growth has to come from Space Systems, and the Q4 launch line looks modest.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 launch revenue fell about 30% q/q and the stock was flat on the print, so launch softness has not been punished when Space Systems carried the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: Launch logs are public, but no preview I read gave a Q3 or Q4 launch count, and the Q3 guide already embeds the Q3 count, so that part sits inside the guide. The part that could matter is Q4: if it were priced, previews would flag a Q4 launch-revenue step-down, and none do.
findings.independence: Mission-count releases: https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Rocket+Lab+Successfully+Launches+16th+Electron+Mission+of+2026%2C+Deploys+Earth+Observation+Satellite (16th of 2026, 09-11); 12th of 2026 on 06-26/27 per the company release summarised at https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/rocket-lab-ten-owl-of-ten-mission-for-synspective-launch; 6th of 2026 on 03-28 per https://rocketlabcorp.com/missions/missions-launched/daughter-of-the-stars/. Q4 timing per https://www.trefis.com/stock/rklb/articles/623715/what-sent-rocket-lab-stock-higher/2026-11-07 (100th mission NET 11-14).

findings.finding: The worst Neutron news was pre-released by 8-K on 2026-10-14: first launch moved to 2027 with no date, after voids were found in a carbon-composite Stage 1 forward dome, and the stock fell about 11% on 10-15. Since then the company says a replacement forward dome has been built and cured, and an aft dome made with the new process is described as its best yet. The call is the first chance to give a 2027 quarter. A firm H1 2027 date would relieve the stock; vagueness or another test issue would extend the drag.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Each Neutron slip announced outside a print (2025 to 2026, then to 2027 on 10-14) drew a large negative day, about -11% on 2026-10-15. On the 2026-08-10 print the 'window is narrowing' language drew -0.04%.
findings.why_not_priced: The delay itself is priced: it is in the 8-K and the stock fell 11%. What is not priced is the 2027 quarter, which the company has not given. Previews list a firmer date as the key test, so the market is uncertain about it, not positioned on it. Pre-releasing the bad news has historically left the call with less downside on this line.
findings.independence: https://www.satellitetoday.com/launch/2026/10/15/rocket-labs-neutron-debut-now-delayed-to-2027/ and https://www.space.com/space-exploration/launches-spacecraft/rocket-lab-pushes-1st-launch-of-next-gen-neutron-rocket-to-2027 report the delay and the dome fix. The replacement-dome detail comes from 24/7 Wall St citing a company X post: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/09/rocket-lab-jumps-9-ahead-of-earnings-ast-spacemobile-surges-11-on-japan-satellite-venture-with-rakuten-spacex-rises-6/

findings.finding: The equity overhang is spent and the Iridium cash is fully funded. On 2026-09-15 Rocket Lab said it had completed its ATM: $1.944B gross from 29.3M shares, about $66 a share, above today's $58.41. It cancelled the $3.6B secured bridge, and Iridium's $1.775B term loan was amended to stay outstanding behind an unsecured Rocket Lab guarantee. Cash was $2.13B plus $258M of securities at 06-30, before the September ATM proceeds. The money buys the cash leg of an acquisition, not operating distress, and no further raise is needed to close.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print-day history on this line. Previews cite reliance on equity raises and dilution as an ongoing concern (24/7 Wall St, 2026-11-09).
findings.why_not_priced: This is public, but previews still frame dilution as a live risk. If the overhang were fully priced, previews would not list equity reliance as a bear point. Small.
findings.independence: Q2 cash and the $1.53B H1 ATM come from the Q2 release (same company, different document): https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001819994/000181999426000061/rklb-08102026ex991.htm

findings.finding: The run-up into the print is sector beta, not news. RKLB fell 12.2% on 11-05 in a post-election sell-off of high-beta tech, rose 15.4% on 11-06 with no filing (Redwire +16.5%, Planet +10.4% the same day) and rose about 9% more on 11-09 with the space group (Firefly +12%, Planet +12%, SpaceX +6%). That is about +27% from the 11-04 close in three sessions, into a print with downside skew of +9.4. Peer Redwire reported a Q3 revenue miss on 11-04 and fell 19.8%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-10): the stock moved -0.04% on a broad beat. The trefis note says the stock has fallen after some past beats. The baseline's 5d run-up is +12.18% against a 20d of -11.11%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is in the price by definition. The point is that a bounce of this size raises the bar, since a guide-midpoint print may not hold a sector-driven gain. If the bounce were rooted in RKLB news, there would be a company filing or contract for 11-06 to 11-09, and there is none.
findings.independence: https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/11/09/rocket-lab-jumps-9-ahead-of-earnings-ast-spacemobile-surges-11-on-japan-satellite-venture-with-rakuten-spacex-rises-6/ (11-09 sector rally). The baseline skew is +9.44.

findings.finding: The target being bought has weakened, and Rocket Lab will guarantee its debt. Iridium's Q3 2026 (2026-10-20) showed revenue +8% to $245.7M, but operating income ex the $103.9M Aireon gain fell about 55% y/y to $31.6M per one analysis. OEBITDA was $135.6M against $136.6M and net leverage is 4.2x, on a $1.775B term loan that Rocket Lab USA will guarantee at close (mid-2027). Analysts on the call may press on deal value; the stock consideration is collared.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on a print. The deal announcement in June 2026 came during the slide from the $150 high.
findings.why_not_priced: Iridium's print is public, and RKLB previews do not mention it. It does not touch RKLB's Q3 or Q4 numbers (closing is mid-2027), so it only matters if the call is asked about it. This is a proxy, and small.

findings.finding: Insiders sold under 10b5-1 plans into the drawdown: Form 144s on 2026-11-02 and Form 4s on 2026-11-03 under a plan adopted 2026-06-03, following CFO Spice's sales (Form 4 dated 10-02) and CEO Beck's roughly 3.28M-share sale disclosed 2026-07-08. These are pre-planned, not discretionary.
findings.why_not_priced: It is on EDGAR and scheduled under a plan, so it says little about the print. Filed for completeness.

outside_window.finding: Firefly Aerospace (FLY) reports Q3 2026 after the close on 2026-11-10, the last session of RKLB's window. Previews flag an Alpha Flight 8 slip into Q4 and a 2026 guide of $420-450M. A peer read-through for launch names lands after RKLB's exit close.
Electron's 100th mission, not before 2026-11-14, is a milestone headline after the window.

baseline_tension: The findings net to zero against a +9.4 downside skew and a sector-driven 27% three-session bounce. The guide-beat pattern leans up and the run-up leans with the skew, so p_up sits just under 50.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name sold its Q2 EBITDA beat and record backlog flat): EBITDA/margin beat-pattern finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4, and backlog finding cut from +0.5 to +0.4.

Lesson 6 (verify the bar): the revenue bar is two agreeing sources plus the guide, so it stands; the EPS bar is disputed (-0.07 against -0.02), so nothing is sized on EPS. This was already so in the draft and is now stated in the bar.

Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest of about 7.3% of float and about 2 days to cover was checked before the negatives; it is not crowded, so no shrink. The positioning finding agrees with the skew and keeps its size.
Lesson 4 (financing is a question): the ATM was already signed positive after asking what it buys (the Iridium cash leg; bridge cancelled), so nothing changed.
